- buffer_overflow（缓冲区溢出，CWE-787/120）：数组或缓冲区的越界写/读，长度校验缺失、差一错误、格式化输出无长度限制。
- data_race（多线程竞争，CWE-362）：线程之间或线程与中断之间共享的状态在锁外或无同步地被读写，包括临界区过早退出、检查与使用分离。
- memory_leak（内存泄漏，CWE-401）：rt_malloc / rt_calloc / rt_strdup / RT_KERNEL_MALLOC / rt_object_allocate 等取得的内存在某条可达路径上失去引用而未释放。
- command_execution（命令执行漏洞，CWE-78）：操作者之外来源的字符串（目录项名、文件内容、其他子系统传入的设备名/路径等）未经校验被拼进命令行并交给 msh_exec() / system() 执行。

C/C++ semantic review checklist (not additional findings):
- evidence: Scanner findings are candidates, not verdicts; zero findings is not a safety proof. Read the complete function and callers before classifying. For each candidate, verify reachability, exact API semantics, guards and the target CWE. Try to refute the candidate using bounds, validation, ownership or synchronization already present. Report a concrete path and trigger, not just a dangerous function name. Keep out-of-scope issues separate.
- bounds: For a destination of capacity C, calculate the maximum written bytes including the final NUL. A successful fgets(dst,n,...) stores at most n-1 bytes plus NUL, not n bytes plus a newline plus NUL. strcspn on that valid string returns at most its length; replacing its terminating NUL is within bounds. Check failed reads separately, without inventing an overlong successful read. strcpy/strcat require strlen(prefix)+strlen(suffix)+1 <= C; use actual literal lengths, not the capacity of their declared arrays. strncat(dst,src,n) appends min(n,strlen(src)) bytes plus NUL after strlen(dst); strncpy and snprintf are bounded by n and the destination capacity, so n=strlen(src) is safe when strlen(src) < remaining space. Width W on scanf %s/%[ needs W+1 destination bytes; %c does not append NUL. Distinguish reads from writes.
- commands: CWE-78 requires attacker-controlled shell syntax reaching an executable command. Trace source -> transformations -> validation -> shell sink. Fixed-format %d/%u output is an integer representation, not the original input string: empty input, failed numeric validation or integer overflow alone does not prove shell injection. Enumerate the actual allowed characters and follow rejection/return branches; if even the fixed command prefix is rejected, that sink may be unreachable. Do not call path traversal, argument injection or arbitrary hypothetical undefined behavior OS command injection without a demonstrated shell-syntax path. Conversely a blacklist must cover all shell syntax; checking one metacharacter or bounding the input length is not sufficient.
- concurrency: CWE-362 requires conflicting accesses to shared state or a shared external resource without adequate synchronization. Identify the accesses and the lock covering each. Do not infer a race from pthread_create, sleep, volatile or a missing return check alone. Inspect mutex initialization and lock failure paths: shared accesses after an unsuccessful lock must not proceed unprotected; state the feasible failure condition explicitly. A success guard around shared accesses prevents that failure-path race. A signal handler calling a non-async-signal-safe mutex function can deadlock (CWE-479/833); that alone is not evidence of concurrent unprotected accesses. Invalid unlock and cancellation cleanup are separate issues unless an actual conflicting-access path is demonstrated.
- reachability: Report a defect only for a feasible path in the analysed program on which the faulty operation actually executes with a triggering value. Evaluate global constants, global variables, macros and helper functions that control branches (for example a constant that is always 5 or a function that always returns 1) instead of treating them as unknown. Follow data across functions, files, function pointers, structs and static globals to every call site. A sink or helper without its own check is not a defect when every call site in the analysed code passes a value proven safe on that path; a missing defensive check alone is a hardening note, not a finding. Values from fgets/fscanf/recv/argv/rand or other external input are attacker-controlled unless validated on that same path.
- indexes: For an array of N elements an index is safe only if 0 <= index < N on that path. A lower bound check alone does not protect an untrusted index, but a constant or validated index below N is safe even when the sink checks only the lower bound. For loops, compute the last iteration value and the element count actually written. Decision rule: list an array access in findings only if you can name a concrete out-of-range index value that reaches it on a feasible path. If every value reaching the access is in range (for example a constant 7 for a 10-element array), it is not a finding even when the sink checks only the lower bound; mention the missing upper-bound check in the summary as hardening. If your own reasoning says the current path is safe, the item must not appear in findings.
- null_pointer: Name the concrete source that makes the pointer NULL on the reported path (NULL assignment, failed allocation/lookup, or a NULL argument) and show that the dereference is reached without an intervening non-NULL guarantee. A dereference in a callee is safe when every caller passes a valid object. Checking for NULL after the dereference does not protect it.
- ownership: For CWE-401 track each allocation identity through aliases, reassignments, swaps, helpers, return paths and loops. A free of a different allocation is not a release of the original. Show a successful allocation path on which ownership is lost or never released after its effective lifetime. Returning ownership to a caller or using stack storage is not by itself a leak. Do not conflate a null dereference, double free or use-after-free with a leak.
